spots.name: Burj Khalifa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Burj Khalifa is a megatall skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Designed by the SOM architectural firm, it is the world's tallest structure, with a total height of 829.8 m and a roof height of 828 m (2,717 ft).

spots.name: Museum of the Future
spots.summary: Museum of the Future is a building located in the Financial District of Dubai, UAE. The museum, with 7 floors, is dedicated to exploring the future of science, technology, and innovation.

spots.name: Dubai Creek
spots.summary: Dubai Creek is a natural saltwater inlet of the Persian Gulf in Dubai. It extends about 9 miles (14 km) inwards and forms a natural port that has traditionally been used for trade and transport. The creek ranges from 200 to 1,200 metres in width while the average depth is about 6.5 to 7 metres.

spots.name: Dubai Museum
spots.summary: Dubai Museum is the main museum in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is located in the Al Fahidi Fort, built in 1787 and is the oldest existing building in Dubai.

spots.name: Dubai Fountain
spots.summary: The Dubai Fountain contains a choreographed fountain system located on the 12-hectare (30-acre) artificial Burj Khalifa Lake, at the center of the Downtown Dubai development in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

spots.name: Bur Dubai
spots.summary: Bur Dubai is a historic district in Dubai, located on the western side of the Dubai Creek. The name is a reference to the traditional separation of the area from Deira by the creek.

spots.name: At the Top
spots.summary: At The Top, Burj Khalifa is a series of observation decks on the 124th and 125th floors of the Burj Khalifa which opened to the public on 5 January 2010.

spots.summary: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood is a historic district in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

spots.name: Grand Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Mosque is a mosque in Dubai, Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is located between the textile souk and the Dubai Museum close to a small stream in the Bur Dubai area. Originally built in 1900, demolished and built again in 1960, it then underwent a further rebuilding in 1998.

spots.name: Jumeirah Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Jumeirah Mosque is a mosque in Dubai, Emirate of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Construction began in 1975 and the mosque opened in 1979; the mosque is built in a combination of historical Islamic architectural styles, including Fatimid and Mamluk.

spots.name: Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo
spots.summary: The Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo is a public aquarium located in the Dubai Mall. It is the biggest aquarium in Dubai and one of the largest in the world. It has the largest glass tank viewing panel at 107 feet wide and 27 feet tall.

spots.name: Dubai Spice Souk

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dubai Spice Souk or the Old Souk is a traditional market in Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE). The Spice Souk is located in Deira, in eastern Dubai, and is adjacent to the Dubai Gold Souk. The Spice Souk is in the locality of Al Ras, on Baniyas Street, near the Old Souk abra station on Dubai Creek.

spots.name: Al Seef
spots.summary: Al Seef or Al Seef Khor is a 1.8 km waterfront promenade along the bank of Dubai Creek in the Al Fahidi neighborhood of Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

spots.name: Iranian Mosque, Bur Dubai

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Iranian Mosque Hosainia is a Twelver Shia hosainia located near the old Textile Souk in the Bur Dubai district of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Built in 1979, the mosque is also known as Ali Ibn Abi Talib Mosque, in honor of Ali Ibn Abi Talib, the central figure of Shiism.

spots.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Library (MBRL) is a large library in the Al Jaddaf locality of Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on Dubai Creek that opened to the public on 16 June 2022.

spots.name: Il Primo Dubai

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Il Primo Tower is a supertall residential skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Built between 2017 and 2023, the tower stands at 356 m (1,168 ft) tall with 79 floors, currently sharing the fifth spot on the list of the tallest buildings in Dubai with the Gevora Hotel.

spots.name: Dubai Coffee Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dubai Coffee Museum is a museum about coffee located in the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood of Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It focuses on the history of coffee, coffee culture, and the working conditions of coffee plantation workers.

spots.name: Dubai Coins Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Coins Museum in Dubai, also known as "The Coins Museum in Bur Dubai," is located in the Emirate of Dubai in the United Arab Emirates in Al-Bastakia, Bur Dubai.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church, Dubai

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holy Trinity Church is an inter-denominational Christian church in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is part of the Chaplaincy of Dubai, Sharjah and the Northern Emirates. It was founded on 5 April 1970, on the land granted by the Emir of Dubai, Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum.

spots.name: Camel Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Camel Museum is a museum dedicated to species of camels and is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The museum displays the important and traditional history of the Arab World and is one of Dubai’s most visited buildings.

spots.name: Museum of the Poet Al Oqaili

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of the Poet Al Oqaili is a museum located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates dedicated to the Saudi-born poet Mubarak bin Hamad bin Mubarak Al Manea Al Oqaili.

spots.name: Rashid Stadium
spots.summary: Rashid Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is currently used mostly for football and rugby matches. The stadium holds 8,015 people. For AFC Asian Cup 2019 stadium was expanded with temporal stands to 12,056 seats. It was built in 1948.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Dubai Municipality Museum

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Dubai Municipality Museum is a heritage site located in the Emirate of Dubai. Established in 1957, it housed the headquarters of Dubai Municipality until 1964, when the municipality moved to a new building on Al Maktoum Street.

spots.name: Sharjah Maritime Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sharjah Maritime Museum is an archaeological museum focusing on marine life that was an essential part of Sharjah's heritage and development. The visitor can see exhibits on pearl hunting, fishing, maritime trade and models of wooden dhows, including a pearl fishing boat, fishing equipment and diving tools.

spots.name: Dubai Ferry trip
spots.summary: The Dubai Ferry makes a sightseeing circular trip to Jumeirah Beach (deep sea side) or to the Floating Bridge (toward the creek). There are also a one way trips towards Dubai Marina at 1pm and 6pm (duration: 2 hours).

spots.name: Saeed Al Maktoum House
spots.summary: Another very historic building built in 1894 now converted into a museum and contains artefacts and images of the old town of Dubai. It was the residence of the Saeed bin Maktoum bin Hasher Al Maktoum, the former ruler of Dubai.

spots.name: Al Ahmadiya School and Heritage House
spots.summary: Built in 1912, Al Ahmadiya School was Dubai's first school and has now been nicely restored. It would be a stretch to call the exhibits of old reed pens and diplomas fascinating, but they've tried pretty hard, and if nothing else, the air-con and clean toilets may come in handy. The attached heritage house is a traditional Emirati-style home built in the 1890s.

spots.summary: Large collection of swords, daggers, riffles, from several centuries.

spots.summary: a historic building home to royal family members built in 1916 and now converted into a museum. It provides good glimpse to old infrastructure of Dubai.

spots.name: Crossroad of Civilization Museum

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Museum includes a lot of artefacts and old books, including a Gutenberg Bible and a curtain of the door of Kaaba from 1543 AD.
